sources.entry: PlugNPlayMac - A script to automate tasks when connect a device to your Mac

summary.one_liner: A shell-script automation that opens and closes chosen Mac apps when an external monitor is connected or disconnected, gated on a specific Wi-Fi network.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a set of shell scripts that run when a Mac is connected to a specific external monitor. The main script opens configured apps (MonitorControl, Elgato Stream Deck, Google Drive, and others in the author's setup) and closes them on disconnect. A separate config file sets which apps to open, which monitor names and Wi-Fi networks trigger the script, and the battery charge limit. The script uses caffeinate to prevent sleep and bclm to limit battery charging, with a Swift file included for battery limiting. An installer copies files to their paths, and a .plist launches the script at startup. Logs are written to /tmp/plug.and.play.mac.log.
use_cases: Auto-launch apps when plugging a Mac into a monitor at home
Close apps automatically on monitor disconnect
Prevent Mac sleep with caffeinate while docked
Limit MacBook battery charging with bclm
Run startup automation via launchd plist
Restrict automation to a specific home Wi-Fi network
how_to_run: Grant Full Disk Access to /bin/bash and /usr/local/bin/PlugNPlayMac/blcm in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access
summary.notable:
["Replaces Amphetamine with the preinstalled caffeinate tool to reduce background apps", "Wi-Fi network check so apps only open at home, not at a similarly named office monitor", "Shortcut for Apple Shortcuts app to toggle functions from the menu bar", "Battery charge limit via bclm, with 80/100 limits on Apple Silicon and 50-100 on Intel"]</notable>
<parameter name="caveats">["Requires macOS Ventura or higher and manual Full Disk Access setup plus a reboot", "bclm on Apple Silicon only supports 80 or 100 charge limits; Intel supports 50-100", "Tested only on a few specific MacBook Pro models; the README says installation still involves manual steps"]
